title: Selfing, Inbreeding, and Inbreeding Depression
objective: Explain how selfing changes genotype frequencies, exposes recessive alleles, increases line uniformity, and can reduce vigor or fertility.
coreScience: Selfing mates a plant with genetically female pollen derived from itself or otherwise allows self-fertilization. Under an ideal diploid single-locus model, heterozygosity is expected to halve with each selfed generation. The genome does not become instantly homozygous, and different regions fix at different times because of recombination, selection, viability, and structural variation.

Inbreeding exposes recessive alleles and can reveal hidden defects in vigor, fertility, development, disease response, sex expression, and seed quality. Inbreeding depression is the decline in performance caused by increased homozygosity for deleterious alleles and loss of favorable heterozygous combinations. Its magnitude differs among populations and traits. Selection can remove some severe defects, but “purging” is not guaranteed and may narrow diversity.

An S1 family is a population of selfed offspring from one parent, not a clone of that parent. It can segregate widely when the parent is heterozygous. Selfing can help reveal genotype, create mapping populations, and develop lines, but it should be paired with population size, family testing, and backup conservation. Do not interpret short-term uniformity in a few plants as genetic stability.
cultivationRelevance: Track selfing generation separately from filial generation, compare each selfed family with the parent and outcrossed checks, and record losses rather than discarding them from the analysis.
measureAndRecord: Parent ID and heterozygosity; selfing method; S generation; seed set and germination; family size; vigor, fertility, sex and abnormality rates; trait variance; molecular homozygosity; selected families and preserved backups.
misconceptions: S1 seed is genetically identical to the mother.
Selfing always creates a stable line in one generation.
Inbreeding depression affects every Cannabis population equally.
evidenceLimits: Heterozygosity decline is an expectation; realized fixation and depression depend on starting genotype, selection, linkage, viability, and population size.
